stories.headline: Bonn climate talks signal momentum but leave climate vulnerable nations on the lurch
stories.summary: The UN climate talks in Bonn concluded with momentum behind the transition away from fossil fuels, but developed countries' failure to address adaptation finance sparked disappointment. The two-week talks ended with unresolved issues, including climate finance, adaptation support, and emissions reductions, ahead of the COP31 climate summit. Sharp disagreements between developed and developing countries persisted, with little progress on the stocktake and deadlock on adaptation. Despite some progress on just-transition talks, the lack of urgency and insufficient progress under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change have fueled calls for reform and legal action to address the climate emergency. The talks highlighted the ongoing struggle between developed and developing countries to make meaningful progress on climate action.

stories.headline: Survivors of wartime rape share stories of trauma and survival
stories.summary: Survivors of wartime rape are sharing their stories of trauma and survival, highlighting the long-lasting consequences of sexual violence used as a weapon of war. A survivor of the 1994 Rwanda genocide, Solange Bigiramana, now lives as a stateless person in South Africa, having faced rape during the conflict. In Ukraine, experts are working to help heal those who suffered trauma from rape used as a weapon of war by Russia, with support from foreign donors. However, in some countries, justice for rape survivors remains elusive, with few convictions for civil war-era crimes. In one instance, only two convictions have been handed down 16 years after the war ended, leaving many survivors feeling frustrated and met with official indifference. Sexual violence continues to target women and children in conflicts worldwide.

stories.headline: Injuries reported as two trains collide north of London
stories.summary: A collision between two trains occurred north of London on Friday, resulting in at least one fatality and injuring dozens of people. The incident happened approximately 60 miles (100 km) north of London, according to British Transport Police. One person, a driver, was killed in the crash. Emergency services responded to the scene, with multiple injuries reported. East Midlands Railway confirmed that emergency services were dealing with the incident, which occurred between London's St Pancras and another location. The Health Minister acknowledged multiple injuries, with several people seriously hurt. British Transport Police are investigating the incident, which involved two trains colliding about 100 kilometers north of London. The exact cause of the collision is not yet known, with authorities working to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

stories.headline: “This Weight Is Too Heavy”: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie Speaks Out on the Death of Her Son and Euracare Hospital’s Response
stories.summary: Renowned author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has spoken out about the death of her one-year-old son, Nkanu Nnamdi, alleging medical negligence by Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital in Lagos. Adichie's son died earlier this year, leaving her and her husband with immense grief. She has publicly shared a letter addressed to the hospital, accusing them of negligence in her son's death. Adichie claims the hospital is attempting to cover up their role in the incident. The author's statement comes months after her son's passing, as she seeks accountability for the circumstances surrounding his death. Euracare Hospital's response to the allegations has not been disclosed. Adichie's public statement marks her first comments on the matter, as she navigates her grief and demands answers from the hospital.

stories.headline: Unpatchable 'usbliter8' Exploit Breaks Apple A12 and A13 SecureROM Boot Chain
stories.summary: Security researchers at Paradigm Shift have disclosed an unpatchable exploit called "usbliter8" that affects Apple's A12 and A13 chipsets. The vulnerability is a hardware bug in the USB controller, allowing arbitrary code execution on devices powered by these chips. The exploit breaks the SecureROM boot chain, enabling access to the device's SRAM. A working proof of concept was made public on June 18, 2026, following coordinated disclosure with Apple Product Security. The exploit supports A12, A13, S4, and S5 system-on-chips. As it is a hardware issue, Apple cannot patch it with a software update, leaving devices with these chipsets vulnerable. The technical details of the exploit have been published, providing insight into the vulnerability and its implications for device security.

stories.headline: Microsoft confirms Windows 11 26H2, urges IT admins to prepare for release
stories.summary: Microsoft has confirmed Windows 11 version 26H2, now available to Windows Insiders in the Experimental channel. The release will be delivered as an enablement package for systems sharing the 24H2/25H2 servicing lineage. This update is expected to be the next major free update for all Windows users, bringing improvements to Explorer, camera control, and AI. Microsoft is urging IT admins to prepare for the release, which is slated to ship this fall. The company is currently testing Windows 11 preview builds, including new Beta and Experimental builds, as part of the 26H2 version. Microsoft announced the update on June 19, 2026, and is encouraging users to test the new version to ensure a smooth rollout. The 26H2 version is part of Microsoft's yearly update cycle, with the goal of providing a seamless experience for users.

stories.headline: Here’s everything new in Wear OS 7 for the Pixel Watch
stories.summary: Google is rolling out the Wear OS 7 update to the Pixel Watch 2, 3, and 4. The update brings improved battery life, enhanced media controls, and a new Live Updates feature that allows users to track live events directly on their wrist. Additionally, users can manage media across their connected speakers and devices. The update also introduces a new interface and notification system. Further upgrades, including Gemini features, are expected to debut later this year. The Wear OS 7 update is available for installation on eligible Pixel Watch devices, offering a range of new features and improvements to enhance the user experience. The update is part of Google's efforts to improve the functionality and performance of its wearable devices.

stories.headline: Thoughts on Image Playground in iOS 27, The Intrigue Found With Spatial Reframing, Where Is Apple’s Generative AI Line in the Sand?
stories.summary: Apple's iOS 27 introduces Image Playground, a feature allowing users to create high-quality images in various styles using generative AI. The update also includes Spatial Reframing, which uses AI to simulate a repositioned camera perspective, generating content to create the illusion. However, Image Playground has received criticism for producing cartoon-like images with typical AI flaws, such as extra limbs or fingers. The feature has been compared unfavorably to other image generation tools, with some considering it to be of poor quality. The introduction of generative AI in Apple's ecosystem raises questions about the company's line in the sand regarding acceptable use of this technology. As Apple continues to develop and refine Image Playground, it remains to be seen how the company will address these concerns and balance innovation with quality and user expectations.

stories.headline: [Ghana's Caleb Yirenkyi credits 'intensity' in training for Black Stars success
stories.summary: Ghana's teenage midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi credited intensive training for his stoppage-time goal that secured a 1-0 FIFA World Cup win over Panama on June 17. Yirenkyi stated that the team's training sessions, characterized by high intensity, played a significant role in his match-winning performance. He emphasized the importance of teamwork, saying "it's not just me, it's everyone helping each other." The midfielder also praised Ghana's backroom staff for their support, particularly during the hydration break, which benefited the players. Yirenkyi's goal helped Ghana weather sustained pressure from Panama, ultimately leading to their victory. The FC Nordsjaelland player remains humble, expressing his desire to continue contributing to the team and country.

stories.headline: [Collin Morikawa rebounds at U.S. Open despite ‘uncomfortable’ back injury
stories.summary: Collin Morikawa is competing at the U.S. Open despite an ongoing back injury that has been affecting him for some time. The world's No. 10-ranked golfer has undergone MRIs and received treatment, but the issue persists. Morikawa has stated that his back is "uncomfortable" and he is unable to hit one particular shot due to the injury. Despite this, he remains in contention to win the tournament after two rounds. This year, Morikawa has finished inside the top 10 in half of the events he has played, demonstrating his ability to perform at a high level even while dealing with the injury. Morikawa's condition has been managed, but he has acknowledged that it is an ongoing issue that he is learning to adapt to. He continues to compete at a major championship, showcasing his resilience and skill.

stories.headline: [US Open: Wyndham Clark hails 'boring' golf for building big lead at Shinnecock Hills and step towards major 'redemption'
stories.summary: Wyndham Clark has built a 4-shot lead at the US Open with the lowest 36-hole score at Shinnecock Hills. Clark credits his "boring" golf for the strong performance, seeking major "redemption." He led after day one, with Matt Fitzpatrick and Rory McIlroy in the chasing pack. Clark's strategy has paid off amid changing conditions at Shinnecock Hills. The US Open is being held at Shinnecock Hills Golf Club in Southampton, New York, with Clark aiming to maintain his pace. He has set himself up for a potential major win, having seized on the opportunities presented by the course's conditions. Clark's lead is significant, and he will look to extend it in the remaining rounds. The tournament continues, with Clark's performance being closely watched by fans and competitors alike.

stories.summary: Ghana's teenage midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi scored a stoppage-time winner to earn Ghana a 1-0 win over Panama in their 2026 FIFA World Cup opener. The 20-year-old midfielder made history by scoring in the 95th minute, securing a dramatic victory for the Black Stars. The match, played at Toronto Stadium, was closely contested, with Ghana forced to play the second half with intensity. Yirenkyi's goal, his first international goal, came in the fifth minute of stoppage time, stunning Panama and giving Ghana a valuable win in Group L. Yirenkyi credited the team's intensity in training for the success, and his goal announced him on the biggest stage, making him a highly rated prospect. The win marks a strong start for Ghana in the tournament.

stories.headline: [Ghana's Caleb Yirenkyi credits 'intensity' in training for Black Stars success
stories.summary: Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi scored a 95th-minute winner to secure a 1-0 victory over Panama in their 2026 FIFA World Cup Group L opener. The match-winning goal, which came at BMO Field in Toronto, was the result of intense preparation on the training pitch, according to Yirenkyi. The win marked a perfect start to Carlos Queiroz's campaign and ended Ghana's six-game winless streak. Yirenkyi's goal also broke Asamoah Gyan's long-standing World Cup record. The young midfielder has reaffirmed his commitment to the national team, stating his readiness to operate in any role assigned to him. Black Stars captain Jordan Ayew has called for patience and protection for Yirenkyi, following his match-winning display. The victory gives Ghana a vital three points in the group stage. Yirenkyi plays for FC Nordsjaelland and has made a significant impact in Ghana's World Cup campaign.

stories.headline: TMC, BJP supporters clash at Kolkata airport ahead of Abhishek Banerjee's arrival
stories.summary: Tension flared at Kolkata Airport as TMC and BJP supporters clashed ahead of Abhishek Banerjee's arrival from Delhi. Banerjee, a TMC MP, had met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in Delhi before returning to Kolkata. The clash occurred at the arrival gate, with TMC supporters alleging that BJP workers arrived with eggs to hurl at Banerjee. Additionally, TMC claimed that a BJP worker was carrying arms with the intent to harm the MP. The incident escalated into a physical confrontation between the two groups, highlighting the ongoing political unrest in the region. The clash has sparked a political fallout, with both parties trading allegations against each other. The incident is under investigation, with reports of the altercation widely covered in local media. Abhishek Banerjee's safe arrival was ensured despite the tense situation.

stories.headline: Dogs only bark, but tigers hunt: Eknath Shinde's warning to Uddhav Sena camp
stories.summary: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde issued a warning to the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) camp, stating "dogs only bark, but tigers hunt." This comes amid speculation of a potential split in the Shiv Sena (UBT) as six Lok Sabha MPs are reportedly in touch with Shinde's camp. The MPs may meet with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Shinde in New Delhi. Tensions have been rising between the two factions, with a senior Shiv Sena (UBT) leader using abusive language against suspected rebel party members during a press conference. Shinde's faction has indicated that its doors are open to Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs who wish to join, fueling speculation of possible defections from Uddhav Thackeray's camp. The rift between the two factions has been escalating, with accusations of corruption and power struggles.

stories.headline: Uddhav Thackeray Duel Features Tigers, Dogs And 'Sholay'
stories.summary: Uddhav Thackeray, leader of the Shiv Sena (UBT), has called a meeting with his party's MLAs amid speculation of "Operation Tiger," a potential defection of MPs to the rival Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde. Thackeray recently met with his nine party MPs, with four attending in person and five online. The meeting comes as six of the nine MPs are expected to join Shinde's faction. The development has led to a war of words between Thackeray and Shinde, with Thackeray accusing the BJP of secretly trying to stop unity among "Marathi parties" and Shinde hitting back, accusing Thackeray of abandoning Hindutva. The crisis poses a fresh challenge to Thackeray's leadership of the Shiv Sena (UBT).

stories.headline: Help hospitals in Gaza and West Bank, Palestine envoy urges India
stories.summary: The Palestinian envoy to India has urged the country to provide urgent aid to hospitals in Gaza and the West Bank, which are facing critical shortages of life-saving medicines and supplies. The envoy highlighted the "mass destruction" of Gaza's infrastructure, including the collapse of essential services like sewage systems, leading to widespread health issues. The Palestinian healthcare system is on the "verge of total collapse" due to the ongoing conflict and financial pressures. The Embassy of the State of Palestine in India has appealed for medical supplies under India's humanitarian initiative, seeking uninterrupted delivery of humanitarian and medical assistance to Palestinians. The envoy's appeal comes amid a worsening healthcare crisis in Gaza and the Occupied West Bank, with the embassy warning of a potential collapse of the healthcare system.

stories.headline: The Globe and Mail] war disgrace cripples the U.S. and elevates China This war has brought about a significant change in global geopolitics
stories.summary: A significant shift in global geopolitics has occurred due to a recent war, with the US experiencing a decline and China gaining prominence. The US redirected a carrier strike group from the South China Sea to the Middle East prior to the war with Iran, and is now moving air defenses from Asia to counter Iranian drones and rockets. The ongoing US-China trade war has also sparked concerns of a global economic slowdown, prompting the International Monetary Fund to lower its 2025 growth forecast from 3.3% to 2.8%. The war has led to a realignment of US military resources, potentially creating an opportunity for China to expand its influence in the region. The economic implications of the trade war and the war's impact on global politics continue to unfold. The US's diminished presence in the South China Sea may have long-term consequences.

stories.headline: [Livemint] America’s loss to Iran has set the stage for fundamental shifts in global geopolitics Uncle Sam has bestrode the world as a superpower since World War II, but its defeat by a non-nuclear middle power like Iran will have global ramifications
stories.summary: The US defeat by Iran has significant global implications, potentially altering the geopolitical landscape. As a superpower since World War II, America's influence is being eroded by the ongoing conflict. The war is damaging US relations with other countries, exacerbating tensions already heightened by President Donald Trump's policies. The consequences of this loss are uncontrollable and irreversible, risking a permanent US presence in the Middle East. This, in turn, may redefine the strategic balance in regions such as the Korean Peninsula. The shift in power dynamics could have far-reaching effects, as the US struggles to maintain its global dominance. The conflict's outcome is likely to impact international relations, security, and diplomacy, with the US facing challenges in regaining its lost influence and credibility. The situation may lead to a significant rearrangement of global power structures.

stories.headline: [ThePrint] Geopolitics is back. We are again grappling with 19th-century questions Strategic thinkers now grapple simultaneously with the return of war and the weaponisation of everything
stories.summary: Geopolitics has returned as a dominant force in international relations, with strategic thinkers grappling with the resurgence of war and the weaponization of various aspects. The term "geopolitics" was previously considered unfashionable, but it has made a significant comeback in the post-COVID period. The world is witnessing a fundamental transformation, with the US hegemony being reevaluated. Professor Michael Hudson argues that the concept of US decline is misleading, as it implies a cyclical pattern of rise and fall. Instead, the focus has shifted to strategic autonomy, reconfiguring public-private partnerships to align with national security goals. The return of spheres of influence is also underway, but with a different dynamic than during the Cold War era, as Cold War binaries no longer apply. This new landscape is characterized by information warfare and cognitive geopolitics.

stories.headline: [The Manila Times] UN climate chief warns against backsliding amid geopolitics
stories.summary: UN climate chief Simon Stiell warned against backsliding on climate efforts amid rising geopolitical tensions. Recent talks in Germany made some progress, but were marred by disagreements over climate finance, with petro-states pushing back against proposals. The talks were a precursor to the COP31 summit, where countries will negotiate further climate actions. Stiell's warning comes after a year of extreme weather disasters, which have heightened calls for rich nations to compensate poor countries for climate-related damages. The issue of climate finance is expected to be a major point of contention at the COP31 summit, with African countries demanding faster climate action and greater support from wealthier nations. The UN has stressed the need for urgent action to cut emissions and mitigate the effects of climate change.

stories.headline: Stock Market Highlights, June 19: Sensex settled 607.08 pts, dragged 154.90 pts Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights - Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 19
stories.summary: The Indian stock market benchmark indices ended lower on June 19, 2026, after a five-day rally. The Sensex dropped 607.08 points to 76,803, while the Nifty fell 154.90 points to 24,013.10. The decline was led by the Nifty IT index, which fell 4% due to Accenture's reduced sales growth forecast. IT stocks were heavily impacted by global pressure, causing them to drop sharply. Despite recovering from the day's lows, the stock benchmark indices concluded the day lower. The decline marked a reversal from the previous five-day rally, with the market reacting to global cues and sectoral pressures. Oil prices also edged higher amid geopolitical tensions, adding to the market's volatility. The Indian stock market's performance was closely watched, with investors reacting to the global developments and their impact on the domestic market.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex closes over 600 points down, Nifty50 above 24,000 - not just IT stocks, HDFC Bank & RIL also drag down indices India Business News: Stock market breaks winning streak: Indian equity benchmark equity indices, BSE Sensex and Nifty50, snapped their five-session winning stre
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices, BSE Sensex and Nifty50, snapped their five-session winning streak, with Sensex shedding 607 points and Nifty settling at 24,013.10. The decline was not limited to IT stocks, as major players like HDFC Bank and RIL also dragged down the indices. The Sensex dropped over 600 points, while Nifty50 remained above 24,000. This downturn follows a recent trend of volatility, with the Sensex previously gaining 347 points and the Nifty closing above the crucial 24,000 mark just days ago. The IT sector was particularly affected, with stocks like Infosys and TCS tumbling after Accenture's weaker FY26 guidance. The market's decline was also influenced by global jitters and a rise in India VIX.

stories.headline: Sensex Tanks 607 Points, Nifty Slips Below 24,050 IT stocks drag markets lower after Accenture's weak outlook; geopolitical concerns add pressure.
stories.summary: Indian stock markets ended lower on June 19, 2026, with the Sensex falling 607 points and the Nifty slipping below 24,050. The IT sector led the decline, plunging 6% after Accenture cut its revenue guidance, triggering a sharp sell-off in stocks like Infosys and TCS. Geopolitical concerns, including renewed US-Iran tensions, added to the market pressure. However, pharma and banking stocks helped limit the downside. The Sensex decline was as much as 750 points at one point, while the Nifty dropped below 24,000. The market sell-off wiped out recent gains, with the Nifty ultimately closing 155 points lower. The weak outlook from Accenture and geopolitical concerns led to broad profit booking across equities, resulting in a significant decline in the Indian stock markets.

stories.headline: Stock Market Crash Today: Sensex tanks 910 pts, Nifty 50 below 24,000 - 5 reasons why The Sensex plunged more than 900 points to fall below the 76,500 mark, while the Nifty 50 dropped over 200 points, slipping below 23,950.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Sensex plunging over 900 points to fall below 76,500 and the Nifty 50 dropping over 200 points to slip below 23,950. The US imposition of tariffs on Indian goods sparked investor concerns, contributing to the decline. Other factors, including FII selling, rupee weakness, and negative global cues, also played a role. The Nifty IT sector fell nearly 1.5% due to concerns over global tech spending, while Nifty Auto, FMCG, Bank, and Financial Services indices declined between 0.3% and 1%. The broader markets were also under pressure, with the Sensex and Nifty shedding over 1% each. The escalation of the US-Iran war and rising crude oil prices further intensified selling pressure on key indices. The market ended with the Sensex at 76,802.90 and the Nifty at 24,013.10.

stories.headline: Starbucks Cuts UK, Hong Kong Office Jobs in Restructuring Effort
stories.summary: Starbucks Corp. has laid off corporate workers in its London and Hong Kong offices as part of a restructuring effort. The move aims to give third-party licensees more control over running stores outside of North America. In Hong Kong, approximately 60 positions, or about 20% of staff, were cut in the office overseeing the Asia-Pacific region, excluding China and Japan. The London office also saw job cuts, although the exact number is not specified. The restructuring effort shifts more responsibility for international operations to third-party licensees, allowing them to have greater latitude in managing stores. The layoffs are part of Starbucks' efforts to streamline its international business operations. The Seattle-based company is making these changes to improve efficiency and adapt to changing market conditions.

stories.headline: DEA Judge Issues Order Laying Out Process For Marijuana Rescheduling Hearing Starting This Month
stories.summary: A DEA judge has issued an order outlining the process for a marijuana rescheduling hearing, set to start this month. The judge has ruled on which witnesses will participate and laid out the procedure for the administrative process. The hearing is part of the Trump administration's cannabis rescheduling process, which has been delayed several times. Recently, the DEA announced that the public hearing on the proposal to reschedule marijuana would be pushed back to the first quarter of 2025. However, the judge has also ordered the DEA to respond to allegations that it opposes the Biden administration's marijuana rescheduling proposal. The hearings have been delayed due to legal challenges, pushing back reform for at least three months. The DEA judge's order sets the stage for the rescheduling hearing, which will consider the classification of marijuana under federal law.

stories.headline: Ivanhoe Mines: A Recovery Year That Could Become A Platform Year
stories.summary: Ivanhoe Mines has announced significant developments, marking a potential turning point for the company. In Q1 2026, despite a $2 million loss, Ivanhoe generated $191 million of adjusted EBITDA, with $158 million attributable to Kamoa-Kakula. The company has completed its debottlenecking program at the Kipushi Zinc Mine ahead of schedule and under budget, achieving fresh production records. Additionally, Ivanhoe has completed three major project milestones at the Platreef Platinum-Palladium-Nickel-Rhodium-Gold-Copper Mine, including the construction of Shaft #3 and commencement of earthworks on the Phase 2 concentrator site. These milestones position the company for potential growth, transitioning from a recovery story to a platform story with a large-scale cash engine in operation. Ivanhoe's recent announcements also include the results of voting for the election of directors during its Annual General and Special Meeting.

stories.headline: Ecuador issues strategic power infrastructure call
stories.summary: Ecuador has issued a call for strategic power infrastructure development, enabling the responsible use of nuclear energy for power generation, research, and medical isotopes production. The government is evaluating a transfer mechanism with state-owned Corporación Eléctrica del Ecuador (CELEC) for a fixed annual payment of around $60 million. This move aims to address the country's energy vulnerabilities, following devastating rolling blackouts in 2024. CELEC has been working to ensure reliable operation, investing $8.5 million in maintenance interventions across the National Transmission System in 2025. The development of nuclear energy infrastructure is part of a broader effort to strengthen Ecuador's energy sector, with the US supporting long-term engagement and strategic relationships. The project also involves partnerships with international companies, including a potential alliance with a Chinese firm to repair and maintain infrastructure.

stories.headline: Nobel Prize winner John Jumper quits Google DeepMind after nearly a decade; set to join Anthropic
stories.summary: John Jumper, a Nobel Prize winner and VP at Google DeepMind, is leaving the company after nearly a decade. He announced his departure to join rival AI firm Anthropic, citing a need to recharge before making the move. Jumper won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his work on AI. His departure highlights the intense competition for top AI talent, with startups like Anthropic competing with established companies for skilled engineers. Jumper's move is the latest example of Silicon Valley talent shifting to new AI companies, underscoring the rapidly evolving landscape of the industry. He will join Anthropic after taking time off, marking a significant change in his career after nearly nine years at Google DeepMind.

stories.headline: What Is Z AI? The Chinese Startup Shaking Up the AI Race With GLM-5.2
stories.summary: Chinese technology company Z.ai, formerly known as Zhipu AI, has launched GLM-5.2, an open-source AI model that rivals GPT-5.5 at a lower cost. The 753-billion parameter large language model is designed for autonomous coding and engineering tasks. GLM-5.2 is positioned as a significant leap forward in reasoning and software engineering capabilities. The model is engineered to dominate "long-horizon" tasks and is considered the strongest open-source coding model currently available. Z.ai's release of GLM-5.2 is seen as a major development in the AI race, with the company's stock surging following the announcement. The open-source model is expected to provide a more affordable alternative to closed-source models, with Z.ai's launch marking a significant milestone in the company's efforts to establish itself as a major player in the AI industry. GLM-5.2's capabilities are expected to have a significant impact.

stories.headline: OpenAI Weaponizes ChatGPT Ads in Korea as IPO Engine Revs Up
stories.summary: OpenAI has confirmed the expansion of its ChatGPT advertising pilot program to South Korea, making it the sixth market to feature ads. The program allows selected brands to display sponsored content within ChatGPT for users in the country. The ads will be limited and target adult users on the Free and Go plans, while paid tiers like Plus, Pro, and Enterprise will remain ad-free. This move is part of OpenAI's efforts to expand revenue ahead of a potential IPO. The company had previously tested ads in the US and later expanded to Canada, Australia, and other markets. The introduction of ads in South Korea marks the latest step in OpenAI's strategy to monetize its popular chatbot platform. The expansion is expected to help the company generate more revenue as it prepares for a potential public offering.

stories.headline: Z AI just launched GLM-5.2, an open-source AI model that rivals GPT-5.5 at a fraction of the cost
stories.summary: Z.ai has launched GLM-5.2, a 744B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with a 1M-token context window, MIT-licensed weights, and two reasoning-effort levels. Released on June 13, 2026, GLM-5.2 is Z.ai's flagship open-weights LLM, topping BridgeBench reasoning at 42.8. It operates at a fraction of the cost of US frontier models, approximately 1/10th, and runs at 300 tokens per second. The model is designed for long-horizon tasks, marking a significant improvement over its predecessor GLM-5.1. Z.ai, a Beijing-based lab, published GLM-5.2 with open-source weights, allowing for widespread access and use. While official benchmarks against models like GPT-5.5 are not yet available, GLM-5.2's capabilities and cost-effectiveness are expected to have a significant impact on the AI landscape. The launch comes amid global developments in AI regulation and export controls.
